(b) Considering the winter mood drops you’ve experienced, keeping your workspace near a sunny window and taking short breaks outside during daylight hours can help maintain focus. Even 10–15 minutes of natural light can make a difference for seasonal affective disorder.
(c) Since you’ve noticed your energy dips in the winter, you might try starting the day with a few minutes under a light therapy lamp before work. Pair that with a brisk indoor stretch or walk to help counteract the low-light sluggishness from seasonal affective disorder.
(d) If you find your energy dips when spending more time indoors, try beginning your day with some light stretching or a brief workout. Pairing that with a healthy breakfast and short breaks for movement can help maintain focus and alertness.
